family.description: This family has been characterised as 3-octaprenyl-4- hydroxybenzoate carboxy-lyase enzymes [[cite:PUB00020511]]. This enzyme catalyses the third reaction in ubiquinone biosynthesis. For optimal activity the carboxy-lase was shown to require Mn2+ [[cite:PUB00020511]]. This entry represents the central RIFT-related domain.
family.name: 3-octaprenyl-4-hydroxybenzoate carboxy-lyase Rift-related domain

causal_graphs.limitations: Does not measure native fungal flux, isolated-domain sufficiency or the complete atomistic trajectory. UbiX supplies cofactor and is not assigned this decarboxylation. Reference taxonomy is not the expression host.

evidence.explanation: Original supplement S5b, PDF p12 plot and main mutagenesis Results; deposited 6R30 sequence confirms L439G. Ledger S3c.

edges.mechanism: Adding BsD raises vanillate conversion from about 5.8% with BsC alone to 100% in both mixed-complex replicates. Residual C-alone activity is retained, not rounded to absence.
edges.subject: add_d

causal_graphs.family_mapping: BsC reference P94405 sequence 1 maps PF01977 106-308; partner reference C0H3U9 maps PF26358 1-51. Primer evidence supports reference relationship, not full insert or strain identity; species-level taxon only. See Vdc ledger.
causal_graphs.limitations: Active assembly, cofactor occupancy and allostery are not separated. Low C-alone vanillate turnover contradicts an unqualified strict-zero claim; synthetic BsC C-terminal junction remains unresolved.

nodes.label: Add cognate BsD before BsC-prFMN-Mn reconstitution

causal_graphs.scope: Separately purified published synthetic BsC and BsD constructs, mixed before reconstitution; not exact accession-sequence proof.
causal_graphs.title: Adding BsVdcD increases the published BsVdcC preparation's activity

causal_graphs.context: 10 uM ShC plus 20 uM BsD, prFMN/Mn reconstitution; 5 mM separately tested substrates, 18 h anoxic-chamber HPLC, two independent replicates. Noncognate D ratio differs from the 1:1 cognate mixed assay.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a ShC+BsD substrate 1; source data and cross-activation methods; ledger V1.

edges.mechanism: The joint noncognate mixture yields 9.3 +/- 0.3% PHB endpoint conversion; activity is limited but detected in both replicates.
edges.subject: phb_mix

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a ShC+BsD substrate 2; source replicates 1.67053 and 1.70697%; ledger V1.

edges.mechanism: Vanillate conversion is approximately 1.7% in each replicate; do not confuse the rounded SEM of zero with an exact absence of variation.
edges.subject: van_mix

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a ShC+BsD substrate 3; ledger V1.

edges.mechanism: Protocatechuic-acid endpoint conversion is 2.7 +/- 0.3% mean +/- SEM in the noncognate mixture.
edges.subject: proto_mix

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a ShC+BsD substrate 4; ledger V1.

edges.mechanism: Methyl-PHB endpoint conversion is 3.8 +/- 0.5% mean +/- SEM; no independent sufficiency is assigned to BsD.
edges.subject: methyl_mix

causal_graphs.family_mapping: ShC Q9S4M7 sequence 1 has PF01977 106-312. BsD is reference-related to C0H3U9, PF26358, with incomplete synthetic insert verification. Mixed-species assay; no single native taxon or PF01977-only sufficiency asserted.
causal_graphs.limitations: Low endpoint yields do not isolate a matched partner-identity effect or demonstrate the in vivo existence of this pairing. Gallic and syringic products are undetected. Distinguish source mixture from co-purified cognate complexes.
causal_graphs.scope: Recombinant ShC combined with the published synthetic BsD partner, not a native interspecies complex.
causal_graphs.title: ShVdcC with noncognate BsVdcD supports limited product formation

causal_graphs.context: 10 uM BsC plus 20 uM ShD, prFMN/Mn; 5 mM substrate, 18 h anoxic-chamber HPLC, two independent replicates. Authentic standards support product assignment.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a BsC+ShD substrate 1; ledger V1.

edges.mechanism: PHB conversion is 0.9 +/- 0.1% mean +/- SEM, with source replicates 0.94695 and 0.80836%; retained as a low measured endpoint.
edges.subject: phb_mix

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a BsC+ShD substrate 2; ledger V1.

edges.mechanism: Vanillic-acid endpoint conversion is 29 +/- 1.8% mean +/- SEM for this mixed-complex preparation.
edges.subject: van_mix

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a BsC+ShD substrate 4; ledger V1.

edges.mechanism: Methyl-PHB endpoint conversion is 8.9 +/- 0.2% mean +/- SEM. Gallic/syringic/other negative tests remain separate limitations.
edges.subject: methyl_mix

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Reference-related BsC P94405 maps PF01977 106-308, with complete synthetic insert unresolved. ShD Q4R102 sequence 1 is the 68-aa deposited partner, mapping to PF26358 2-42 rather than PF01977.
causal_graphs.limitations: Protocatechuic, gallic and syringic products undetected. Different D ratios and preparation types prevent attributing all yield differences to partner identity alone. Low PHB conversion has unspecified detection limits.
causal_graphs.scope: Published synthetic BsC construct combined in vitro with ShD; whole recombinant proteins, not a native physiological partnership.
causal_graphs.title: Published BsVdcC with ShVdcD yields three low-activity products

causal_graphs.context: Reconstitution ShC 50 uM, ShD 10 or 200 uM, prFMN and Mn 200 uM each. Assays use 0.25 uM C and 100 uM non-degassed PHB, A247 over 3 h; three technical replicates and three independent trend repeats.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2b and complete source Fig 2b time course; stoichiometry Methods; ledger V2.

edges.mechanism: Excess D yields a higher activity plateau; at 90 min approximately 16.5-18.0 uM/min versus 7.0-8.2 with substoichiometric D. It is not evidence that free D alone catalyzes decarboxylation.
edges.subject: excess_d

causal_graphs.family_mapping: ShC Q9S4M7 PF01977 106-312 within a multidomain enzyme; titrated ShD Q4R102 is a PF26358 partner, not a second PF01977 domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Activity does not resolve an exact catalytic assembly stoichiometry or separate binding, assembly and cofactor maturation/occupancy. Different time points are reconstitution-dependent activities, not direct single-molecule transitions.

nodes.label: Increase D:C from 0.2 to 4 at fixed ShC

causal_graphs.scope: ShC at fixed concentration, reconstituted with substoichiometric or excess ShD.
causal_graphs.title: Greater ShVdcD availability increases PHB decarboxylation activity

causal_graphs.context: 90 min exposure, PHB assays at 100 uM in 50 mM NaPi/50 mM KCl pH 6 by A247. After 90 min return to anoxic chamber and add two equivalents prFMN without extra Mn, then immediately reassay; two independent replicates.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2c time course before rescue; source Fig 2c and aerobic decay Methods; ledger V3.

edges.mechanism: Mean measured activity falls from 2.49 s^-1 at 2 min to 0.855 at 90 min. The reported approximate 40-min half-life is not a newly fitted intrinsic cofactor-oxidation constant.
edges.subject: air_time

evidence.explanation: Figure 2c 90+prFMN and source values 2.09035/1.86647; ledger V3.

edges.mechanism: Cofactor addition after air exposure yields mean activity 1.97841 s^-1, about 79.5% of the 2-min mean, without additional Mn. This intervention is a partial rescue, not a direct identification of the inactivation chemistry.
edges.subject: cofactor_addition

causal_graphs.family_mapping: ShC deposited body Q9S4M7 sequence 1, PF01977 106-312, with ShD Q4R102 PF26358. Effect concerns the full cofactor-bearing complex, not an isolated PF01977 region.
causal_graphs.limitations: No chemical identity of an oxidized cofactor lesion or controlled oxygen-dose response established. Rescue is partial and consistent with a cofactor contribution; neither full reversibility nor sole causation is claimed. Opaque tube limits light effects, distinct from AnFdc light assays.

nodes.label: Extend ShCD air exposure from 2 to 90 min
Add prFMN after 90-min exposure and return to anoxic chamber

causal_graphs.scope: Reconstituted and desalted ShCD exposed to air in an opaque open tube; subsequent prFMN addition to the same aged preparation.
causal_graphs.title: Air exposure lowers ShVdcCD activity and added cofactor partly restores it

causal_graphs.context: PHB 50-750 uM, 50 mM NaPi/50 mM KCl pH 6; 45% v/v glycerol or 40% w/v sucrose. prFMN:CD:Mn 0.5:1:2; active protein assumed equal to prFMN after overnight trace-oxygen maturation. Buffer n=3 and each viscosogen n=2 technical replicates; trends in two independent repeats.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4d and source Fig 4d fit values, KSVE methods; ledger V4 retains occupancy and viscosity assumptions.

edges.mechanism: Fitted kcat_app decreases from 0.856 s^-1 in buffer to 0.244 with glycerol; source 95% limits 0.7607-0.9686 and 0.1885-0.3407. This is a measured rate effect, not measured domain closure.
edges.subject: glycerol

evidence.explanation: Figure 4d sucrose curve and source fit values; ledger V4.

edges.mechanism: Fitted kcat_app decreases from 0.856 s^-1 in buffer to 0.341 with sucrose; source 95% limits 0.2518-0.4757 for sucrose. The direction is observed without resolving the molecular cause.
edges.subject: sucrose

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q9S4M7 PF01977 106-312 with Q4R102 PF26358. The proposed interdomain hinge T325/S326 is outside PF01977; the assay does not isolate either domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Apparent kinetic normalization assumes complete UbiX conversion and active-cofactor occupancy. Km confidence intervals overlap. Estimated viscosity and solvent effects cannot uniquely prove a hinge-motion mechanism or exclude noncompetitive solvent effects.
causal_graphs.scope: Whole ShCD-prFMN complex in separate solvent-viscosogen kinetic assays, not direct observation of domain motion.
causal_graphs.title: Glycerol and sucrose lower apparent ShVdcCD turnover

causal_graphs.context: Co-purified WT and V59X complexes, prFMN/Mn reconstitution, 10 uM C, 5 mM substrate, 18 h endpoint HPLC; two independent replicates. PHB/protocatechuate/methyl-PHB yields remain near WT and syringate is undetected in both.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a ShCD and V59X substrate 2; source replicates and 7AE7 identity; ledger V5.

edges.mechanism: Vanillate mean endpoint conversion falls from 100% WT to 91.5 +/- 3.7% V59X, with V59X replicates 87.88321 and 95.19112%. This describes the observed mean, not a demonstrated universal rate deficit.
edges.subject: tail_deletion

evidence.explanation: Figure 2a and source Fig 2a substrate 5 qualify the broad tail-deletion prose; ledger V5.

edges.mechanism: Gallic-acid conversion falls from WT 4.78839/5.79144% to 0/0% for V59X. A small absolute yield difference is loss of the detectable low activity, not uniform retention of more than 90% of WT function.
edges.subject: tail_deletion

causal_graphs.family_mapping: 7AE7 entity 1 equals Q9S4M7, PF01977 106-312; entity 2 equals Q4R102 1-58 versus 68-aa WT. Deleted VIPPIPPLKK belongs to the separate ShD protein; PF26358 core maps 2-42.
causal_graphs.limitations: Yield changes are not proportional changes in catalytic rates. No significance test is inferred from n=2 endpoints; most retained activity does not make the partner wholly dispensable. Assembly/occupancy and local geometry can contribute.

nodes.label: Delete ShD residues 59-68 in V59X complex
Vanillate endpoint conversion relative to WT
Low gallic-acid endpoint conversion relative to WT

causal_graphs.scope: ShCD containing partner variant V59X, deleting ShD residues 59-68; not a mutation in the PF01977 domain.
causal_graphs.title: ShVdcD tail deletion has substrate-dependent effects

causal_graphs.context: The substrate-specificity section reports 6.5 +/- 0.6% syringic-acid turnover versus undetected WT. General substrate scope uses overnight 5 mM endpoints with reconstituted complexes; a separate L182V raw dataset, replicate count and complete insert were not supplied in the inspected files.

evidence.explanation: Substrate-specificity Results and supplement Figure 4 model; the numeric L182V result is absent from all five source-data sheets. Ledger V5 distinguishes text from raw data.

edges.mechanism: The authors report 6.5 +/- 0.6% turnover for L182V versus no detected WT turnover. This scoped reported observation is not an observed atomistic explanation of substrate positioning.
edges.subject: l182v

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q9S4M7 sequence 1 and WT 7AE4/5/7 bodies verify L182 within PF01977 106-312. Mutation is reported and cloning methods describe sequence confirmation, but no deposited mutant sequence/structure is equated with this construct. ShD remains the separate PF26358 partner.
causal_graphs.limitations: Text-only result, not independently inspected raw replicates. Supplement table labels both mutagenesis primers Q5F. The activity gain supports altered specificity but does not uniquely prove greater cavity volume or exclude maturation/assembly effects.
causal_graphs.scope: Published L182V mutation in ShC within the complete ShCD system; experimental result reported in text only.
causal_graphs.title: ShVdcC L182V permits low syringic-acid turnover

causal_graphs.context: Hybrid closed prFMN-binding region and open oligomerization region, 16 Chimera morph models, DFT Int2/Int3Quinoid and Vina docking. prFMN positioning and selected side-chain conformations constrain the model; cofactor, partner and substrate are joint premises.

evidence.explanation: Figures 4b/5, docking Methods and archived model design; ledger V6. Source Fig 4b contains relative docking energies only.
evidence.snippet: domain closure leads to a strained conformation

edges.mechanism: Open models preferentially accommodate Int2 while closure changes its fit; the authors propose that closure exerts strain on the aromatic adduct. This interpretation is not a measured force or captured strain trajectory.
edges.subject: closure_int2

evidence.explanation: Figure 5 proposed mechanism and Figure 4b Int2/Int3Quinoid docking profiles; ledger V6, not AnFdc trapped-adduct transfer.
evidence.snippet: domain closure leads to a strained conformation

edges.mechanism: The proposed closure-coupled rearrangement converts stable Int2 toward Int3Quinoid, whose docked geometry favors more closed models. Neither its rate nor the intervening proton transfers is experimentally resolved in VdcCD.
edges.subject: strained_int2

evidence.explanation: Figure 5 proposed product branch and modeling Results; ledger V6 separates modeled trajectory from observed V1 endpoints.
evidence.snippet: domain closure leads to a strained conformation

edges.mechanism: The authors' scheme completes adduct turnover with phenol liberation and regeneration of the catalytic cofactor complex. Endpoint HPLC observes product but does not establish that this exact quinoid-to-product route was traversed.
edges.subject: quinoid

causal_graphs.family_mapping: ShC Q9S4M7 PF01977 106-312 within the 480-aa enzyme; T325/S326 hinge and L425 are outside this domain. 7AE4/7AE5 are apo closed/open structures. R168 is sequence-verified; R178 labels in main figures and R138 in supplement Figure 3 are inconsistent source labels, not verified Arg residues.
causal_graphs.limitations: Docking energies are not activation free energies. No holo crystal, trapped VdcCD intermediate trajectory or hinge perturbation establishes these steps. Viscosity data are separate observations that do not uniquely identify domain motion; no isolated PF01977 sufficiency or family-wide transfer.

nodes.label: Proposed strained aromatic Int2 within full ShCD
Proposed released phenol product and regenerated cofactor complex

causal_graphs.scope: Computational model of PHB chemistry in full ShCD, based on apo structures, docked cofactor/intermediates and a morphed interdomain trajectory; not an observed sequence of catalytic intermediates.
causal_graphs.title: Proposed ShVdcCD domain closure promotes prFMN-adduct turnover

causal_graphs.context: Apo ShCD structures show the partner interface near ERE-containing loops; mixed-partner activity and V59X retained activity motivate the model. Cofactor and substrate remain required premises for turnover, not independent consequences of D binding.

evidence.explanation: Figure 3b interface and V59X discussion; ledger V6. Physical contacts and endpoint effects remain distinct from demonstrated allostery.
evidence.snippet: maintaining the structure of the key catalytic ERE motif

edges.mechanism: Interface contacts could maintain loop geometry needed for chemistry in the full cofactor-bearing enzyme. The directed stabilization explanation is proposed from structural context, not directly observed as the causal activation route.
edges.subject: partner_interface

causal_graphs.family_mapping: ShC Q9S4M7 PF01977 106-312 includes R168/E273/E278. ShD Q4R102 PF26358 2-42 and its tail are a separate protein. Main-figure R178 is inconsistent with sequence G178; the reference motif contains R168.
causal_graphs.limitations: No direct loop-dynamics assay or selective interface perturbation establishes stabilization as the activity-restoring mechanism. Alternatives include altered assembly, cofactor occupancy and maturation. Zinc association and structural proximity are not sufficient causal proof.

nodes.label: Proposed ShD association at the ShC loop interface

causal_graphs.scope: Hypothesis for how the separate ShD partner enables an active whole ShCD complex; association and activity effects do not alone prove this route.
causal_graphs.title: Proposed ShVdcD stabilization of catalytic loops

record.description: This family has been characterised as 3-octaprenyl-4- hydroxybenzoate carboxy-lyase enzymes [[cite:PUB00020511]]. This enzyme catalyses the third reaction in ubiquinone biosynthesis. For optimal activity the carboxy-lase was shown to require Mn2+ [[cite:PUB00020511]]. This entry represents the central RIFT-related domain.

evidence.explanation: VdcCD substrate, partner, oxygen, viscosity and variant assays are now assessed separately from the proposed dynamic mechanism. Sh deposited bodies are mapped; complete synthetic Bs constructs remain unresolved.

discussions.notes: Continue ScFdc and PMID28753302, EcUbiD, AroY, HmfF, HudA and later maturation/specificity studies, plus VdcCD native-system and construct follow-up. Preserve the full family and corpus scope; see evidence/PF01977/anfdc-primary-assays.txt and vdcc-primary-assays.txt.
discussions.prompt: Extend the family assessment beyond the mapped AnFdc and scoped VdcCD experimental systems.
discussions.rationale: PF01977 is the central domain of diverse multidomain enzymes; AnFdc chemistry does not establish a universal substrate, partner requirement or native physiological role.

evidence.explanation: Figures 2/3 and supplement S4/S5 support scoped adduct and activity observations; F437/L439 belong to PF20696. The computed Int1-open state and specific proton-transfer sequence are not directly measured trajectories.

discussions.notes: Extend the remaining substrate/inhibitor and small-analogue graphs after their individual assay review. Resolve solution-MS incubation details, active-cofactor normalization, construct sequences and the limits of domain transfer. Do not combine E282Q Int2 and WT Int3 into one observed mutant-independent trajectory. VdcCD docking and partner-allostery graphs remain hypotheses; apo structures and viscosity effects do not measure the proposed catalytic trajectory or isolate PF01977 sufficiency.
discussions.prompt: Resolve intermediate transitions and separate whole-enzyme effects from PF01977-specific chemistry.
discussions.rationale: Trapped adducts, residue perturbations and computed transition states provide different levels of evidence. No isolated PF01977 fragment was shown sufficient for catalysis.

evidence.explanation: Original Figures 5/6/7 distinguish low turnover, absent detectable exchange and apparent kinetics. R173A cofactor maturation and variant-dependent occupancy prevent a simple catalytic-residue inference.
Extended Data 1 has a detector-wavelength discrepancy and Extended Data 8 has a third-panel color-caption discrepancy; neither is silently corrected or mistaken for a new biological result.

Sh sequence verifies R168/G178 despite inconsistent figure labels. Source data retain low C-alone vanillate activity, a nonzero BsCD gallic replicate and loss of low ShCD gallic activity after partner-tail deletion. L182V is reported only in text; active-cofactor normalization and complete Bs insert identity remain unresolved.

discussions.notes: R173 is verified in A2QHE5; position 172 is Ala. F437L is verified in deposited 6R2Z despite the 2019 F439L prose typo. Obtain missing raw assay/construct details; absence of detected product is not proof of zero activity under all conditions.
discussions.prompt: Resolve primary-source label discrepancies while retaining condition-specific negative and residual activities.
discussions.rationale: The 2015 blanket inactivity claim is refined by 2018 residual R173A/E277Q activity; detection methods and cofactor preparation matter.
